belongs_to: 'They collected data from 35 friends and recorded it in a notebook as shown below.' (the 35 answers to 'How many hours a day do you spend watching TV?', tallied later in the page-2 table)
description: A notebook page (cream, faintly ruled paper, dashed blue border, 10 black spiral rings with purple clips along the top edge) full of 35 hand-drawn child faces in pencil outline, scattered over the page. Every face has exactly one teal speech bubble that gives that friend's answer in hours (written 'hr'). Total 35 faces and 35 bubbles. Counted tally of the bubbles: 1/2 hr = 9 bubbles; 1 hr = 13 bubbles; 1 1/2 hr = 7 bubbles; 2 hr = 3 bubbles; 2 1/2 hr = 3 bubbles (9+13+7+3+3 = 35). The fractions are printed as small stacked fractions (1/2 with the 1 over the 2; mixed numbers 1 1/2 and 2 1/2). Bubble values in approximate position order (top band, then upper-middle band, then lower-middle band, then bottom band; left to right inside a band): TOP (8): 1 hr, 1 1/2 hr, 1 hr, 2 hr, 1/2 hr, 2 1/2 hr, 1 1/2 hr, 1 hr; UPPER-MIDDLE (12): 1/2 hr, 1 1/2 hr, 1 hr, 1/2 hr, 1/2 hr, 1 hr, 2 hr, 1 1/2 hr, 1/2 hr, 1 hr, 1 hr, 1 1/2 hr; LOWER-MIDDLE (8): 2 1/2 hr, 1 hr, 1 hr, 1 hr (written vertically as 1 over hr), 1/2 hr (vertical), 2 hr, 2 1/2 hr, 1 hr; BOTTOM (7): 1 1/2 hr, 1 hr, 1/2 hr, 1 1/2 hr, 1/2 hr, 1 hr, 1/2 hr. The faces are all different children (boys and girls, different hair styles, some looking sideways) with no other data. Bubbles differ in size and tail direction but each reads as plain 'n hr'.
unclear: The tally per answer value (9, 13, 7, 3, 3) was counted twice and equals the counts already used in the LP v6 (and 9+13+7+3+3 = 35 friends); the reading ORDER of the bubbles listed above is approximate because the faces are scattered, so only the tally is exact.
One bubble near the middle-right is written vertically as '1 / hr' (value 1 hr); one at the lower middle as vertical '1/2 / hr' (value 1/2 hr).

section: Food Wastage in the School Canteen
belongs_to: 'Rani stays in a residential school. Her school's dining hall displays the amount of food wasted and the number of children the food could have fed.'
description: A picture of a blue-framed notice board on two black legs. Heading 'NOTICE BOARD'. Teal text: 'Take all you can eat.' 'Eat all you take.' Then in dark red handwriting: 'Yesterday's food wastage was' with the number 13 written in blue in a white box followed by '- Kg,' and 'Which could have fed' with the number 25 written in blue in a white box followed by '- people.' So the board shows 13 kg and 25 people.
unclear: The board says 13 kg could have fed 25 people (about 2 people per kg), which is not the same ratio as the question 4 rule (1 kg feeds 3 children); this is as printed.

section: Food Wastage in the School Canteen

Vertical scale numbers 0 to 9 written to the left at thin black horizontal lines (one line per number 1 to 9; 0 is the baseline); no vertical axis title other than the panel title.
